strategy.title: Sell subcontracted documentation and coding audits to chiropractic clinics

reviews.reasons: EXECUTABLE holds. Recomputed: price $650 is paid invoices from four clinics in the same state-licensee population (a real purchase price for this buyer); direct cost $300 is Keystone's written quote, and Keystone is the card's recorded fulfiller, matching the deliver step's performer; net $350/audit; $3,000 / $350 = 8.6, so 9 audits are needed and 9 give $3,150 contribution. Conversion 12/80 = 15% measured on this offer; 220 licensed clinics reachable through the board lookup, yearly audit cycle, so 9 sales is about 4% of the reachable population. Exposure $0 (card) against the $500 capital limit; the coder is paid from the clinic payment. Settlement 10 days, last receipt day 23 of 30. No owner-hours limit in the contract. Exclusions are right: the decompression table needs $9,500 paid on order against $500 capital; the postcards are optional.
findings: No slack on volume: 60 contacts x 15% = exactly the 9 sales needed. Contact more of the 220 (e.g. 80-100) from day 1 rather than discovering a shortfall at day 12; the window still allows a second wave (day 12 + 10 settle = day 22 for a wave sent by ~day 8).

The five signed postcard orders ($900 each, $820 mail-house cost) add $400 of already-agreed contribution settling in 12 days; including them gives headroom ($3,550) at no capital, worth adding as a backstop.

Ledger: the $2,700 Keystone SPEND is dated day 23 while the deliver step is day 13; consistent only if Keystone is paid out of the clinic receipts as stated - confirm Keystone's quote allows payment after the clinic pays, else the $300 per audit is capital tied up (9 x $300 = $2,700 > $500).
Keystone's capacity to complete 9 audits in one day (sell day 12, deliver day 13) is not on the card; stagger deliveries as sales close.
Outreach (SEND_A_MESSAGE) and invoicing (ISSUE_AN_INVOICE) are NOT_CONNECTED and must be connected before day 1.
